Maria: Kicking off load-priming for us-south-1 today at 09:30 PT. Plan: quick smoke -> steady ramp -> 2h soak at target QPS -> 2 short spikes. Runbook excerpt below. Need one oncall + one infra eng to watch GPU queues.

Ashwin: I can monitor autoscaler/HPA and the cluster autoscaler. What are our acceptance targets?

Maria: Target p95 < 200ms for /generate (1-token avg), steady GPU util 65–75%. Start with concurrency=8, batch_size=32 on A100s. If pending queue > 250, throttle the load generator.

Devon: Can you paste the quickchecks and load commands?

Maria: ```bash
# smoke checks
kubectl --context us-south-1 get pods -n inference -l app=model-server -o wide
kubectl top pods -n inference | grep model-server
curl -sS https://us-south-1.redwood-internal/test/health | jq .

# local load generator (vegeta example)
vegeta attack -targets=targets.txt -rate=250/s -duration=30m | vegeta report
```

Sara: FYI reserved capacity in us-south-1 is 48 GPUs (6 pods at current config). Do we want to pull overflow from the shared preemptible pool?

Liam: We have ~64 preemptible GPUs in us-central available for bursts. Proposal: route non-critical soak traffic to preemptible pool (max 30%) and keep steady critical traffic on reserved pool.

Ashwin: Autoscaler suggestions: HPA target CPU 60%, custom metric pending_requests_per_pod < 20, CA scale-down-delay=15m, scale-up-cooldown=30s. Set maxReplicaIncrement=10 for faster ramps.

Tony: Network note: egress to S3 goes out NAT-gw with ~5Gbps baseline. If we see spill to S3 for KV checkpoints, that could spike latency — watch NAT metrics.

deploy-bot: load-priming job started by Maria at 2026-03-18T09:32:10Z. job_id=lp-20260318-0932

Devon: Observing p95 ~320ms after 20m, GPU util 82%, pending queue ~140. Scaling is sluggish — pods are coming up but model init takes ~90s.

Ashwin: If model init is slow, enable KV warmup and bump initialReplicas. Try `--warmup=kv-prefix` and set initialReplicas=4 -> 6. Also check taints/tolerations delaying placement.

Maria: Applied initialReplicas=6 and enabled KV warmup. Also reduced per-pod concurrency to 6 to avoid saturating single GPU.

Liam: Routing updated: 30% of soak traffic now directed to preemptible pool using route policy `soak-preemptible-fallback`.

Devon: After changes: p95 back to ~180ms, GPU util ~68%, pending queue ~60. Continuing soak for 1h and will run two 10m spikes at 200% ramp.

Sara: Cost heads-up: preemptible consumption estimated +$900/hr while running. Approve for up to 3h?

Maria: Approve for 3h max. Enable billing alert: budget/region/us-south-1 > $2k/day.

Tony: Post-soak handoff checklist: add final metrics to /docs/regions/us-south-1/runbook, create a follow-up ticket if p95 >250ms sustained for 15m, and schedule a tuning session with SRE. Include CA logs and HPA events.

Ashwin: Also recommend adding a canary route with 1% traffic to verify future model rollouts in-region before full promotion.

Maria: Thanks — will publish final runbook edits and metrics in this thread once soak completes.
